Calm Systems

By Rowan Hale

A calm system makes its important transitions visible. Operators can tell whether work was accepted, whether it is still running, and which terminal result was recorded without reconstructing the story from unrelated logs.

Durable work also needs one owner for the database change and the queue action. Keeping those effects together makes retries ordinary and turns ambiguous crashes into states that a reconciler can resolve.

The final ingredient is a bounded retention policy with enough recovery time. Capacity metrics then show whether the bound is being honored before storage pressure becomes an incident.
